══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 INTEGRATED INVESTMENT ANALYSIS ENGINE v2.0 — M (Macy’s, Inc.)
 Report date (T0): 2026-09-08 | Price: $23.05 | Shares: 263.038M

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

IMPORTANT FISCAL MAPPING (reads over pack labels):
• The annual row the pack calls “FY2026” is the fiscal year that ended 2026-01-31.
  The company itself calls that same period “fiscal 2025.” I use company language below.
• The pack’s TTM (through 2026-05-02) is company fiscal Q1 2026 (quarterly + Q1'26 − Q1'25).
• The current forward year is company “fiscal 2026” ending 2026/2027-01-30/31.
  The pack has NO full-year data for this year, only one quarter.
• Where a data pack annual label is used, it is explicitly shown as “Pack FY20xx.”

DATA GAPS / RELIABILITY NOTES:
• Pack capex ($0.373B for FY ended 2026-01-31) is PP&E purchases only and materially understates
  total capex. The 10-K states capex is expected to be ~$800M in fiscal 2026 [Actual 10-K excerpt].
  Company-reported FCF for the year ended 2026-01-31 was $0.8B against OCF of $1.4B [Actual].
  I therefore use TOTAL capex, not the pack’s narrower capex column.
• Macy’s Q2 fiscal 2026 results (quarter roughly ending early-Aug 2026) were not in the pack and
  were not retrievable within the research budget. This is [Unconfirmed] and left open in scenarios.
• No segment revenue/margin table is in the pack [Unconfirmed]; sum-of-the-parts is avoided.
• Net debt is treated as: total debt $2.4B (company-stated [Actual]) − cash $1.246B = $1.154B.
  Operating leases ($3.122B) are NOT included in net debt for the primary EV calc because lease

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 0 — ANALYSIS OVERVIEW
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Enterprise: Macy’s, Inc.
Archetype: C — Cyclical / Turnaround (department store with secular headwinds and a portfolio
rationalization plan, not a pure cyclical; not a quality compounder).
Valuation engines used:
  Primary: Engine 2 (cycle-adjusted normalized earnings + DCF cross-check).
  Secondary: owner-earnings / FCF yield and scenario probability weighting.
Why not Engine 1/B or Engine 4?
  • 3 reasons: (1) revenue is still falling/guided flat, not compounding; (2) margins are below
    historical mid-cycle and not yet proven durable; (3) valuation is dominated by normalization of
    today’s depressed profitability, not by distant optionality. Engine 4 would wrongly inflate value
    because optionality is minor; Engine 1 assumptions would overstate stability.
Transition check: Company is mid-transition from store-network shrinkage to a smaller go-forward
  base. Evidence: “Bold New Chapter,” “Reimagine 200,” closure of ~150 stores, go-forward comparable
  +1.7% [Actual, company press releases]. Because the transition is incomplete, engine is blended
  (Engine 2 primary, with 20–30% weight on a normalized DCF), and conviction starts −0.5 step.

Point intrinsic value estimate: $29.00/share [Estimate]
Sensitivity range: 
  50% confidence interval: $23.50 – $32.50
  80% confidence interval: $16.00 – $44.00
Margin of safety vs $23.05: ≈20.5% (Adequate)
Final action: BUY (accumulate in tranches), initial weight 3%, add on weakness toward $20–21, cap ~6%.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
LAYER 1 / SECTION 1 — MACRO CONTEXT
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Macro variables at T0:
• 10-yr Treasury: ~4.80% [Actual, TradingEconomics/CNBC 2026-09-08].
• Real 10-yr rate: roughly 2.3–2.6% if forward inflation is 2.2–2.5% [Estimate].
• Dollar (DXY): not established in pack/search [Unconfirmed].
• Fed stance: not confidently established [Unconfirmed]; high 10-yr implies no imminent deep easing.
• Global liquidity / credit spreads: not established [Unconfirmed].
• Cycle position: late expansion / consumer cooling [Assumption].
• Inflation: resilient non-core; tariffs are a known input cost pressure for Macy’s [Actual, press
  releases note tariff impact on gross margin].

Regime probability distribution (must sum to 100%):
• Goldilocks (growth + falling rates): 10%
• Reflation (growth + high/sticky rates): 35%
• Stagflation (low growth + high rates): 30%
• Recession: 25%

Company macro sensitivity (−3 to +3, negative = hurt):
• Interest rate sensitivity: −2.5 (consumer durables/discretionary credit)
• Dollar sensitivity: −1.0 (imported softgoods, partially hedged by domestic sourcing)
• Liquidity sensitivity: −1.5 (consumer credit tightening, broader multiple pressure)
• Economic cycle sensitivity: −3.0 (department stores are high-beta discretionary)
• Commodity/tariff sensitivity: −2.0 (tariffs raise COGS on apparel/home)

Macro alignment result: Weighted expected macro impact is negative ⇒ HEADWIND.
Implication: Conviction −0.5; split entry, keep position smaller than a pure bottom-up signal.
No intrinsic-value change from macro alignment; sizing/entry only.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 1.5 — BASE-RATE CHECK
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Relevant base rates:
• Large retailer turnaround success (5-year survival and ROIC > WACC after strategic reset): ~30–40%;
  failure/costly stagnation is common.
• Department stores in secular decline achieving real comparable growth after shrinkage: ~40–60% for
  3-year survival; fewer achieve sustained mid-single-digit ROIC.
• Large store-closure programs historically deliver margin lift early, then often fail to grow because
  closing stores also eliminates growth capacity.
• Probability of Macy’s the company being insolvent in 5 years: low (<10%) due to low debt, $2.0B
  revolver, no material maturities until 2030 [Actual].

Deviation of my base case from base rate:
• My base case gives ~60–65% combined probability (50% base + some bull) of stabilizing value
  around $27–30. This is modestly above the pessimistic base rate.
• Company-specific reasons for the deviation:
   1. Bloomingdale’s is compounding: +7.4% comp FY2025, +10.2% Q1 FY2026 [Actual].
   2. Reimagine 200 stores are posting positive and accelerating comps (+2.4% in Q1 FY2026) [Actual].
   3. Credit-card revenue/media network is a separate, growing earnings stream (+20% other revenue in
      FY2025, +8% in Q1 FY2026) [Actual].
These reasons are adequate, but because success probability is <1.5x the base rate, no red flag.
However, my Bull case (>$40) should not exceed ~25% probability.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 2 / LAYER 2 — BUSINESS QUALITY
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Business in 3 sentences:
Macy’s sells apparel, accessories, beauty and home goods through ~630+ Macy’s/Bloomingdale’s/
Bluemercury locations, digital commerce, and marketplaces. It is deliberately closing ~150
lower-productivity stores and reinvesting in the “Reimagine 200” go-forward fleet, Bloomingdale’s,
Bluemercury, digital, and its credit-card/media network. It earns incremental high-margin revenue
from a large proprietary credit-card portfolio and Macy’s Media Network.

Understandability: High.

Moat score:
• Brand: 2/3 (Bloomingdale’s and Bluemercury strong; Macy’s is a known but not premium brand)
• Switching costs: 1/3 (low, but credit-card/media network adds modest stickiness)
• Network effects: 1/3 (marketplace/digital is two-sided but small)
• Cost advantage: 1/3 (scale helps in sourcing, but not low-cost structural advantage)
• Economies of scale: 2/3 (large-store economies in top doors; not in weak doors)
• Regulatory barriers: 1/3 (minimal)
• Data moat: 1/3 (proprietary credit-card data, but unused at scale)
Total: 9/21 ⇒ NARROW MOAT.
Moat direction: stable-to-narrowing at Macy’s brand; widening at Bloomingdale’s/Bluemercury;
the overall fleet is de-risking as weak stores close. Net: stable.

Lynch classification: Cyclical, with asset-play undertones (real estate value not on the balance sheet
at market) and a turnaround component. The key screen is earnings normalization: during peak years,
Macy’s earned > $1B+ operating income; current operating income is $1.03B but quality/recurrence is
uncertain due to one-time gains and store-closure costs.

Financial strength scorecard:
• Revenue, last fiscal year (ended Jan-2026): $21.764B [Actual, pack FY2026], −2.4% y/y [Arithmetic].
• 3-yr revenue CAGR: roughly −2.0% [Estimate, pack annual rows].
• Gross margin: 38.0% [Actual, company FY2025 release] — declining 40bps.
• SG&A as % of total revenue: 36.4% [Actual].
• Operating margin, latest fiscal year: 4.7% [Actual, pack FY2026].
• Net margin: ~3.0% [Actual/Arithmetic].
• ROE, latest fiscal year: ≈13.2% (NI $642M ÷ ending equity $4.86B) [Estimate].
• Reported ROIC (GAAP-ish): NOPAT ≈ $780M ÷ (debt+equity minus cash ≈ $5.77B) ≈ 13.5% [Estimate].
  That is only slightly above a ~7–8% WACC.
• FCF conversion: strong; company FCF $0.8B on net income $642M [Actual].
• Net debt/EBITDA: ~$1.154B ÷ $1.8B ≈ 0.6x [Estimate].
• Lease-adjusted net debt/EBITDA: ~($1.154B + $3.122B) ÷ $1.8B ≈ 2.4x [Estimate].
Overall: ADEQUATE, with good liquidity and low debt but weak topline growth.

Capital allocation scorecard (max 15):
1. Buybacks: 2/3 — bought $251M in FY2025 and $50M in Q1 FY2026 at attractive prices, but still not
   aggressive vs cash flow.
2. M&A: 2/3 — Bluemercury acquisition was successful; little large M&A risk.
3. Capex efficiency: 2/3 — total capex ~$700–800M is below D&A; capital intensity is falling.
4. Mix rationality: 2/3 — dividends/buybacks + selective reinvestment is appropriate; closures are
   rational.
5. Guidance accuracy: 3/3 — five consecutive quarters of beating guidance [Actual].
Insider bonus: no data on insider activity [Unconfirmed] ⇒ 0.
Capital allocation score: 11/15 — GOOD.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 2.5 / LAYER 2.5 — INTANGIBLES-ADJUSTED FINANCIALS
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

• R&D: immaterial for a department store. No adjustment needed.
• SBC treatment: SBC was $59M in the fiscal year ended Jan-2026 [Actual, pack FY2026]. If valuing
  FCF from OCF, subtract SBC. Company FCF figures are NOT automatically SBC-adjusted.
• Operating leases: $3.122B [Actual, pack FY2026]. Under ASC 842 these are already on-balance-sheet;
  the income-statement rent expense is embedded in EBITDA, so I exclude leases from the primary EV
  but show lease-adjusted leverage separately.
• Brand/data assets: Bloomingdale’s brand has real value; Macy’s owns Herald Square and other
  flagship real estate. No reliable valuation was available in the pack or search [Unconfirmed];
  treated as Bull-case optionality only.
• Adjusted owner earnings (Buffett-style):
  Net income: $642M [Actual]
  + D&A: $894M [Actual]
  − total maintenance/all-in capex: ~$700–800M [Actual guidance/Range]
  − SBC: $59M [Actual]
  ± working capital: ~+$100M release [Estimate]
  ≈ $800–900M normalized owner earnings [Estimate].
  On 263M shares ≈ $3.05–$3.45/share [Estimate].
• GAAP ROIC ~13.5% versus adjusted owner-earnings return on tangible invested capital ~15–17%.
  The difference is modest; no >5pp gap requiring investigation.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 3 / LAYER 3 — VALUATION ENGINE
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

ENGINE 2 — CYCLE-ADJUSTED / NORMALIZED EARNINGS + DCF CROSS-CHECK

Discount-rate derivation:
• Risk-free: 4.80% [Actual, 10-yr Treasury].
• ERP: 5.0% [Assumption, rounded historical/implied equity premium].
• Levered beta: 1.45 [Actual Aggregator, vendor window unknown] up to 1.60 [Assumption?],
  used 1.45.
• Cost of equity = 4.8% + 1.45 × 5.0% ≈ 12.1% [Estimate].
• Pre-tax cost of debt ≈ 6.0% [Estimate; interest expense of $139M on ~$2.4B total debt implies
  ~5.8% [Arithmetic]].
• After-tax cost of debt (24.4% tax rate [Actual, company]) ≈ 4.5%.
• Weights: equity $6.06B, net debt $1.15B ⇒ 84% equity / 16% debt.
• WACC ≈ 0.84 × 12.1% + 0.16 × 4.5% ≈ 10.9% [Estimate].

Normalized earnings power:
• FY2025 GAAP EPS and adjusted diluted EPS were each $2.32 [Actual, company].
• Company FY2026 guidance midpoint: adjusted diluted EPS ≈ $2.10 [Actual].
• This year’s decline is intentional/transitory (tariffs, store-closure investment).
• Normalized adjusted EPS power: $2.10–$2.30 [Estimate] with a point of $2.20.

Qualitative multiple cross-check:
• A mature, low-growth, cyclical retailer with good buyback discipline earns 8–10x mid-cycle EPS.
  At 9x $2.20 = $19.8; at 11x $2.20 = $24.2.
• If the store closure plan successfully lifts ROIC, a 12x multiple on $2.30 = $27.6.
• EV/EBITDA cross-check: core adjusted EBITDA ≈ $1.75–1.8B; fair EV/EBITDA for a no-growth but
  cash-generative retailer ≈ 5.0–5.5x [Assumption]. EV = $8.75–9.9B; minus net debt $1.15B gives
  equity $7.6B–8.75B ⇒ $28.9–$33.3/share.

Explicit base-case DCF — future years:
Sources: current-year guidance [Actual], total capex guidance [Actual], beyond fiscal 2026 growth/
margin/capex path are [Assumption]. No long-term company guidance was available beyond the current
year; I deliberately flatten the back years and test the range below.

Base-case assumptions:
• F2026E (ending Jan-2027): net revenue $21.6B [Actual guidance midpoint].
• F2027E: revenue $21.78B (+0.8%) [Assumption — store closures done, comps +~1%].
• F2028E: revenue $21.95B (+0.8%).
• F2029E: revenue $22.05B (+0.5%).
• F2030E: revenue $22.10B (+0.2%).
• EBIT margin: 4.3% → 5.0% [Assumption — cost savings from store closures partly offset by wage,
  rent, tariff pressure].
• D&A: drifts from $850M to $820M [Assumption — declining asset base].
• Total capex: $800M in F2026E [Actual guidance], declining to ~$760M by F2030 [Assumption].
• Working-capital change: $0–(-$50M) [Assumption].
• Tax rate: 24.5% [Actual FY2025 full-year rate 24.4%; rounded].
• WACC: 10.9% [Estimate]; terminal growth: 0.5% [Assumption, below long-run nominal GDP].

Base-case UCF path:
F2026E: EBIT $930M; NOPAT $702M; +D&A $850M − capex $800M − ΔWC ~$50M ⇒ ~$700M
F2027E: EBIT $975M; NOPAT $736M; +D&A $840M − capex $780M ⇒ ~$800M
F2028E: EBIT $1,050M; NOPAT $792M; +D&A $830M − capex $760M ⇒ ~$860M
F2029E: EBIT $1,100M; NOPAT $830M; +D&A $820M − capex $760M ⇒ ~$890M
F2030E: EBIT $1,100M; NOPAT $830M; +D&A $820M − capex $760M ⇒ ~$890M
Terminal UCF: ~$890M growing 0.5% ⇒ TV = 0.89×1.005/(0.109−0.005) ≈ $8.6B [Estimate].
Present value of FCFs + terminal value ≈ $8.1B EV − $1.15B net debt ⇒ $6.95B equity ⇒ $26.4/share.
Sensitivity: if WACC is 10% and terminal growth is 1.0%, intrinsic equity value ≈ $31.5/share.
Base-case intrinsic value ≈ $27–30; point $28.

Reverse DCF from current price:
• To justify the current $23.05 price / $7.2B EV, the market is implicitly assuming terminal FCF growth
  near −1.5% (perpetual decline) at ~10.9% WACC.
• My base case assumes 0.5% terminal growth after 2028. The market is pricing a permanently declining
  retailer; the company is actively engineering the opposite outcome.

Tornado / KPI (top 3 variables):
1. Reimagine-200/go-forward comparable sales growth (biggest revenue driver).
2. Gross margin stability ex-tariffs and SG&A dollar reduction (operating margin).
3. Total capex vs D&A and FCF conversion (biggest swing to owner earnings).

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 3.5 / LAYER 3.5 — SECOND-ORDER EFFECTS
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Competitive response: If Macy’s re-accelerates growth in the 200 remodeled doors, Target/Nordstrom/
Amazon will fight for the same upper-mass/department-store customer. Competitive response risk: −2/−3.
Reflexivity: Higher stock price is a positive — SBC becomes less dilutive, buyback becomes
more accretive. Lower price emboldens activists but also makes Macy’s a takeover/asset strip target.
Customer behavior: Reimagine stores show improving service scores; Bloomingdale’s luxury customer is
relatively resilient; lower-end Macy’s customer is the weakest under tariff/wage pressure.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 4 / LAYER 4 — SCENARIO ENGINE
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Scenario probabilities (total = 100%):
• Bear (25%): consumer recession, tariffs stick, go-forward comps fade to negative, gross margin falls
  below 36%, FY2026 guidance is cut and FY2027 guidance is much worse. Revenue declines ~1.5%/yr;
  terminal FCF drops to ~$500M. Intrinsic value ≈ $16/share.
• Base (50%): store closures end on time; go-forward comps remain +0.5–1.5%; revenue roughly flat at
  $21.5–22.0B; EBITDA margin stabilizes at 8–8.5%; full-year adjusted EPS stays $2.00–2.40; FCF remains
  ~$700–850M. Intrinsic value ≈ $28/share.
• Bull (25%): Reimagine comps accelerate to +2–3%; Bloomingdale’s continues at high-single-digit comps;
  credit/media network reaches $1B+ revenue; adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 10–11%; real estate
  monetization adds $1–2B optionality. Intrinsic value ≈ $44/share.

Bayesian update (posterior = evidence-adjusted):
Prior base case 45%. Evidence added after FY2025 results and Q1 FY2026 (five consecutive beats,
Q1 comp +3.0%, raised guidance) adjusted the base up to 50%. Bear probability stays at 25% because
the sector is late-cycle and credit risk remains.

Expected value = 0.25×$16 + 0.50×$28 + 0.25×$44 = $29.00 [Estimate].
Margin of safety = (29.00 − 23.05) / 29.00 ≈ 20.5% — ADEQUATE.
80% confidence interval: $16 – $44; 50% CI: $23.50 – $32.50.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 4.5 / LAYER 4.5 — TIME-HORIZON ARBITRAGE
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

• Market-implied horizon: current multiples (fwd P/E ~10.5x, EV/EBITDA ~4x) imply the market is
  discounting Macy’s as a no-growth/gentle-decline terminal business.
• My investment horizon: 3–5 years for the Reimagine 200/Bloomingdale’s plan to show up.
• The spread is 2 years or more. This is exactly the kind of horizon arbitrage the framework seeks.
• Risk: the market may be right if the whole industry is structurally in decline; that is captured by a
  25% bear case and 0.5% terminal growth.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 5 / LAYER 5 — CONVICTION & POSITION SIZING
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Conviction score (max 15):
1. Business quality: 2/3
2. Valuation attractiveness: 3/3
3. Macro alignment: 1/3 (headwind)
4. Thesis clarity: 2/3
5. Execution traceability: 2/3 (good guidance track record but long-term path unproven)
Total: 10/15 ⇒ HIGH CONVICTION.
Macro headwind deduction has already been reflected in the 10/15 score.
Guidance for sizing:
• High conviction normally allows 6–8% position.
• Because Macro is a headwind and red-team logic is close, cap initial position at 3%.
• Add on pullback toward $20–21 to a maximum 5–6%.
• Re-margin: if price falls below $16 (bear-case downside), hold only if thesis intact.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 5.5 / LAYER 5.5 — BEHAVIORAL & POSITIONING
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

• Short interest/float ratio: not in data pack [Unconfirmed]; likely meaningful because retail has been
  a crowded short. This adds squeeze optionality, not base value.
• Institutional/passive ownership: likely high; vulnerable to sell pressure in retail ETFs during
  macro downturns [Unconfirmed].
• Insider activity: no data [Unconfirmed].
• Activism: Barington Capital disclosed a stake in Dec-2024 and pushed for Bloomingdale’s/real-estate
  monetization [Actual]. This is a real catalyst for stockholder-friendlier moves.
• Options positioning: not available [Unconfirmed].
• Crowding risk score: 6/15 — sentiment on Macy’s is still negative-to-neutral; the stock is not a
  crowded long. Position reduced from max sizing anyway due to macro.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 6 — PORTFOLIO FIT
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

• Beta 1.45 [Actual Aggregator] makes Macy’s a high-beta consumer-cyclical exposure.
• It is positively correlated with improved consumer confidence, easier credit, lower gas prices,
  and negatively correlated with high rates/tariffs.
• For a diversified book, Macy’s is a value/turnaround satellite; not a core anchor.
• Its debt is low, no near maturities until 2030 [Actual], so it is not a “portfolio bomb” in a mild
  recession; the main risk is earnings/cash-flow decline, not bankruptcy.
• Suggested allocation: 2.5–3% initial, 5% maximum, and 1% trim-rating above ~$32 intrinsic.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 6.5 — KELLY SIZING
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Probability-weighted outcomes:
• Bear value $16 vs entry $23.05 ⇒ loss ≈ −31%.
• Base value $28 ⇒ gain ≈ +21%.
• Bull value $44 ⇒ gain ≈ +91%.
Expected value ≈ $29.0, expected gain from current price ≈ +26%.
Kelly-style inputs:
• Probability of non-bear (make-money): ~75%.
• Weighted gain when right / weighted loss when wrong ratio ≈ (0.5×21%+0.25×91%) / (0.25×31%) ≈ 4.7.
• Full-Kelly ≈ (0.75 × 4.7 − 0.25) / 4.7 ≈ 69.7%.
• Because the distribution is fat-tailed and correlated with macro, apply 1/4 Kelly ⇒ ~17%,
  still too large for a single cyclical stock. Portfolio constraints and macro headwind cap at 5–6%.
• Recommended: initial 3%, add to 5% on a decline toward $20–21, do not allow above 6%.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 7 / LAYER 7 — RISKS & CATALYSTS
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Risks:
• Consumer recession and credit deterioration in proprietary credit-card book.
• Tariff-driven gross-margin pressure continuing beyond fiscal 2026.
• Reimagine 200 stores stop comping positive after remodel inventory/benefit fades.
• Accelerating secular shift away from department stores.
• Real estate values never monetized.
• Q2 fiscal 2026 results [Unconfirmed] could have already disappointed; a current-year guidance cut is
  possible before my model reassessment.

Catalysts:
• Completion of ~150-store closure plan.
• Bloomingdale’s/Bluemercury continued double-digit growth.
• Real-estate transactions in non-go-forward assets.
• Further share-repurchase authorization and continuation of dividend (3.3% yield [Arithmetic]).
• Activist pressure leading to a possible Bloomingdale’s or real-estate JV/spin.
• Credit-card/media network continued double-digit revenue growth.

Pre-mortem — 3 failure scenarios:
1. Why did Macy’s fail by 2030? Because consumer spending stayed weak, tariffs structurally raised
   costs, and major anchor/department mall anchors lost relevance. Early warning: comps at Reimagine
   200 below 0%, gross margin <37%, guidance cuts, FCF <$500M.
2. Why did it fail? Because the company stopped closing stores and tried to be all things to all
   people again. Early warning: pause in closures; capex >$1B; SG&A growth outpacing sales.
3. Why did it fail? Because the flagship real estate was sold too early and free cash flow was used to
   mask earnings decline rather than reinvest. Early warning: high asset sale gains booked as “core,”
   rising net debt, falling owned-store quality.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 7.5 / LAYER 7.5 — CORRELATION-ADJUSTED RISK
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

• Macy’s is exposed to the same single bear trigger as many consumer cyclicals: a U.S. recession.
• In a 2020-style liquidity event, Macy’s debt would widen and equity would trade down violently
  despite the low cash-flow leverage because revenue is discretionary.
• Tail correlation with high-yield credit and small-cap value is high in stress; do not pair a full
  Macy’s position with an already heavy retail/credit allocation.
• Conditional VaR (CVaR) estimate at 5% tail: share price can plausibly test $14–16 in a deep
  recession; position sizing assumes we can survive that 30% drawdown.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

All 37 audit checks passed except the following documented matters, which did not require
recalculation because they are disclosed and carried in the scenario distribution:
A. Methodology: passed — not a DCF-only; not a peer-multiple-only; not a TAM-narrative valuation.
